name: Question 4
problem:
$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}1, & x\in [0,1) \\ x, & x\in [-1,0)\end{aligned}
$$

The above function $F(x)$ is defined on $x\in [-1,1).$ 
Select the correct options below.

| I. | $F(x)$ is continuous on $x\in (-1,1)$ | {{field-1}} |
| --- | --- | --- |
| II. | $F(x)$ is piecewise smooth on $x\in (-1,1)$ | {{field-2}} |
| III. | ${lim}_{x\to -{1}^{+}}F(x)={lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}F(x)$ | {{field-3}} |
| IV. | $f(x)$ is piecewise smooth and continuous on $R$ | {{field-4}} |
worked_solution:
Let's examine the given statements in turn.

- Statement I is $\text{false}.$ The function $F(x)$ has a jump discontinuity at $x=0.$ Its graph is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14229051/assets/2eb2120db83d33d37f1d076f7e3664a21cd1bb97ccd04aeb792cd8e510edf846.png)

- Statement II is $\text{true}.$ The function $F(x)$ is piecewise smooth on $x\in (-1,1).$ It consists of two smooth pieces.

- Statement III is $\text{false}.$ Indeed, we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to -{1}^{+}}F(x)={lim}_{x\to -{1}^{+}}x=-1
$$

and 

$$
{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}F(x)={lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}1=1.
$$

So, ${lim}_{x\to -{1}^{+}}F(x)\ne {lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}F(x).$

- Statement IV is $\text{false}$ since statements I and III are false.

**Note:** The $2$-periodic extension of $F(x)$ to $x\in R$ has the graph shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14229051/assets/c91cf3eea948fdce9a992c77d95bc3c8bc5165ade9e6f17ae5b7e699b0a9be9d.png)

EXPLANATION

Let's examine the given statements in turn.

  • Statement I is false. The function F(x) has a jump discontinuity at x=0. Its graph is shown below.

  • Statement II is true. The function F(x) is piecewise smooth on x∈(−1,1). It consists of two smooth pieces.

  • Statement III is false. Indeed, we have limx→−1+F(x)=limx→−1+x=−1 and limx→1−F(x)=limx→1−1=1. So, limx→−1+F(x)≠limx→1−F(x).

  • Statement IV is false since statements I and III are false.
